alyssa: Heads-up - noticed a canary perf regression after today's merge. short-seq p99 jumped from ~85ms -> ~190ms on the small seq benchmark. Canaries show sustained increase. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

perf-bot: CI alert: runtime/short-seq p99 regression detected. baseline 85ms, current 188ms (+121%). Failing job: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/98765/logs. Suspected commit range: abc123..def456

buildbot: Merge commit def456 (PR #4127) triggered the canary run. Build: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/98765. Artifacts uploaded.

dan: Ok, let's bisect. Suggested range abc123..def456. @mohit @jen can you try reproducing locally? I'll coordinate the bisect if you need help.

mohit: On it. Quick repro command I use for short-seq: ```./tools/run_bench --model gpt-small --seq 128 --runs 200 --mode=latency --kernels=auto```
Also try forcing kernel hints: ```RKERNEL=fast_mem ./tools/run_bench --model gpt-small --seq 128 --runs 200```

jen: I profiled a canary node earlier. Flamegraph shows a large spike in kernel_selector.choose() and a shift to fused_attention_v2 for short sequences. The commit 7f2d looks suspicious (it adjusts kernel heuristics). Snippet: ```kernel_selector.py: choose() +40% CPU, hot path: fused_attention_v2_dispatch```

dan: Can someone try pinning kernel policy to v1 to confirm? env var: REDWOOD_KERNEL_POLICY=prefer:v1

alyssa: Ran that locally: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_POLICY=prefer:v1 ./tools/run_bench --model gpt-small --seq 128 --runs 200` -> p99 back down to ~90ms. So kernel selection change is likely the culprit. :thumbsup:

mohit: Doing a local git-bisect now. Early results point at commit 7f2d9a5 which modified the kernel scoring heuristic. That commit is part of PR #4150.

jen: Note: PR #4150 also tweaked batching heuristic for tiny batches (batch_max default change). Could be an interaction between selection and batching for short-seq workloads. We should test combinations.

mohit: Confirmed with toggles: ```REDWOOD_KERNEL_POLICY=prefer:v1 REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX=8 ./tools/run_bench --model gpt-small --seq 128 --runs 200``` -> p99 ~92ms. With default/new settings (v2 + batch_max=32) -> p99 ~185ms.

dan: Good repro. If kernel pin fixes it, we should revert just the kernel-heuristic part of PR #4150 as a rollback, and follow up to refine heuristics + add perf guard tests.

alyssa: I'm going to roll canary back to the previous release now and notify infra. We can't risk the regression hitting prod.

buildbot: Rollback executed: canary deployed to previous version (deployed at 2026-03-18T14:22Z). Canary metrics back to baseline (p95/p99 within historical variance).

jen: I'll open a revert PR for the kernel-heuristic change and add unit tests + a perf guard for short-seq p99. I'll also add a note in PR #4150 to follow up on batching interplay.

mohit: I'll add an e2e short-seq perf test to our CI perf suite (small model, seq=128, batch sizes 1-32) so this can't sneak by again.

dan: Thanks all — good catch and fast turnaround. Let's capture the bisect steps in the postmortem/notes so reviewers know to run the short-seq bench before merging heuristics changes.

alyssa: Filing a short incident note and linking this thread. Great work, team.
